title: cmd/compile: elide call to runtime.growslice with provable capacity availability

labels.name: NeedsInvestigation
labels.description: Someone must examine and confirm this is a valid issue and not a duplicate of an existing one.

labels.name: compiler/runtime
labels.description: Issues related to the Go compiler and/or runtime.

milestone.title: Unplanned
milestone.description: No plan to fix in any specific release.

body:
Using `go1.12`

Consider the following snippet:
```go
/*12*/	func Append(b []byte) []byte {  
/*13*/		if cap(b)-len(b) > 3 {      
/*14*/			b = append(b, 0, 1, 2)  
/*15*/		}                           
/*16*/		return b                    
/*17*/	}
```

The regions marked in red seem superfluous. At a high-level, we already know that `cap(b)-len(b) > 3` so the check at 0x0037 is entire redundant. Also since there is guaranteed capacity, the code at 0x0069 and on is entirely unnecessary.
